findings.summary: The bootstrap grant does not define how an already-open session acquires or enforces authority for a later move/replacement.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:44–56, 79–85, 130–137 authorize the Hello's requested chunk set once and cache only in that session. Actual replica/mod.rs:346–353 creates a missing chunk on BeginResync; the target can add a new move destination on an existing node/volume session. A session established before that assignment has no matching SessionAssignment, and the design never specifies per-request grant enforcement or a transition to acquire its new role.
findings.fix: Persist the authorized chunk/ref/role/operation set in the accepted session and check it before every creation or reconstruction operation. Define a bounded control-path reauthorization or explicit new-Hello transition when moves add chunks/roles, including operation changes, session supersession, and delayed answers. Do not add metadata calls to ordinary I/O. Test a session predating the move, an ungranted BeginResync, and a stale replacement operation before any store mutation.

findings.summary: The new replica-gate exceeds the concrete release transaction limit.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:59–64 requires an extra atomically bumped gate on release mutations. The current #13 design.md:105–122 permits 118 chunk comparisons plus header and #72 ledger comparisons, exactly 120. Adding the gate makes 121, refused by meta/kv/etcd.go:91–92. #13's sweep concretely emits batches of 118. Repeated release failure prevents reclamation and eventually blocks moves at the release bound.
findings.fix: Recalculate every affected transaction and publish the new exact batch caps, including ConfirmRelease request validation, producer, tests, #72 ledger interaction, ForgetNode/enrollment batches and model adapters. For the existing ConfirmRelease shape, reduce the maximum to 117 if one extra compare suffices; document the complete compare/write table and test boundary and boundary+1 against both backends.

findings.summary: Replacement completion accounts only for current data, leaving snapshot and DR historical completeness unspecified.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:79–85 follows the current Mapped/copy/holes resync and admits the new ref after 'full synchronization'. Actual target.rs:2351–2377 reconstructs only the current chunk. Current #51 design.md:170–199 instead requires every committed historical stage, suppresses live forwarding until lower stages complete, and rechecks the frontier before joining. #58 design.md, Lifecycle and commit, additionally requires committed and pinned roots/receipts on every joiner. #52 contracts.md:43–55 relies on #61 identity plus that completeness to grant a snapshot source.
findings.fix: Define replacement admission's composition with snapshot/root profiles: reconstruct and prove every committed/pinned historical view using the exact #51/#58 transition when those profiles exist, or explicitly refuse the unsupported profile before replacement begins. State which barrier/version proves completion across cuts and takeover, and add caught mutants for joining after current-only reconstruction and accepting a stale historical frontier.

findings.summary: Every-Hello metadata authorization can exhaust memory and starve membership/fencing work.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:44–50 adds paged metadata work for every new Hello but supplies only a page-size bound (:135), with no aggregate pending-session, queued-page, retry, deadline or fairness bounds. Actual net.rs:176–199 spawns accepted connections without a cap, :212 uses an unbounded reply channel; flaminio-metaclient/lib.rs:110–120 serially services one unbounded call queue. A valid target with a retained token can repeatedly open sessions during an outage and queue authorization work ahead of ChangeIsr/refresh/heartbeats.
findings.fix: Specify bounded preauthorization state, active/pending grants and bytes per node/peer/volume, handshake/grant deadlines and cancellation on disconnect/supersession, bounded retry/backoff, and fair scheduling that prevents bootstrap pages monopolizing the metadata worker. Refuse excess sessions without enqueuing work. Test a valid-token Hello flood, stalled metadata, many-page volume and cancellation while existing targets still make bounded control-path progress.

findings.summary: The paged authorization interface states binding requirements without a concrete verifiable cursor/grant protocol.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:59–64 and 130–137 let requests supply after/generation/snapshot_revision and require a fixed full-request digest, but do not define the first-page snapshot acquisition, authenticated/server-owned continuation, generation source, fixed final comparison set, or lifetime/bounds of Mem snapshots. The digest is response-only. 'Do not trust a caller-supplied newer generation' is an invariant, not an implementable mechanism, and KV currently has neither historical reads nor snapshots (meta/kv/kv.go:38–52).
findings.fix: Fix the exact GetAt/ListPage snapshot API and revision semantics and a stateless authenticated continuation or bounded server-owned grant record that binds caller/store/token digest/first epoch/epoch/full sorted chunk set/gate and node revisions. Specify the final O(1) comparison transaction, all gate writers/initialization/no-delete rules, expiry/cancellation/resource reclamation, compacted-revision behavior and restart. Test forged/mixed cursors, changed request sets, generation ABA, compaction and incomplete-page refusal.

findings.summary: The claimed shared replication-v2 bytes conflict with the current snapshot-v2 proposal.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:143–145 says ALPN flaminio-repl/2 and inserts a canonical UUID string before Hello's token, and UUID16 into Fenced. Current #51 contracts.md:160–197 independently fixes HelloV2 tag 0x10, a u16 version=2 and the existing Hello layout 'unchanged thereafter', plus new snapshot request tags and legacy-frame refusal. #72 contains no ReplicaRef/wire-v2 contract at all; its intent.md:53 postpones multiple disks until after #61. Thus 'matching #72' does not settle the actual #51/#61 codec composition.
findings.fix: Provide one exact composed profile/tag/layout table for identity-aware ordinary and snapshot/root sessions, including Hello/Fenced, endianness, UUID representation, ALPN negotiation and old/new cross-decode behavior. Make #61 the actual owner of ReplicaRef rather than claiming an existing #72 definition. Add shared golden vectors for both feature combinations and controlled refusal of mismatched profiles; leave dependencies read-only while recording the exact second-to-land hooks.

findings.summary: Exact-store cleanup is promised but the cleanup authority/storage/RPC schemas remain node-only.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:23, 85–90, 126–148 adds released_refs to ChunkMeta and says #13 releases/fences/tombstones must use refs, without defining header fence-holder refs, tombstone pending/confirmed refs, stored schemas or revised list/confirm request fields. Baseline meta.proto:169–190 identifies tombstones and ConfirmDeletion only by node; #13 design.md:105–153 defines node-only ConfirmRelease/ListReleases and self-IO authorization. The new store must not confirm an unplugged old store, but these builders have no agreed bytes to express that distinction.
findings.fix: Define the complete versioned exact-ReplicaRef cleanup contracts, including header/tombstone records, list responses, confirmation requests, incarnation/revision preconditions, node/ref self-authorization, legacy-field handling, retry and ledger release behavior. Explicitly distinguish possession/deletion of the old UUID from mere current node identity. Add real RPC/adapter tests where a replacement tries to confirm the old ref and an old disk returns after new membership has joined.

findings.summary: The shared response/frame size envelope is deferred although identity fields invalidate its existing formula.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:126–147 adds authoritative ref arrays while retaining node projections, then leaves #80 to 'tighten shared caps if needed'. #80 design.md:29–47 fixes B(N,R) and per-RF caps for node-string memberships; #13 design.md:65–85 adds release/fence-holder terms, and #51 adds catalog bytes. Each ReplicaRef adds nested node+UUID/tag bytes, and exact cleanup refs add more. No new composed formula/caps or rule for including/omitting projections is given.
findings.fix: Compute and publish the concrete combined bound/caps now for the proposed supported profiles, maximum canonical UUID/ID lengths, R+1 membership/move/release/fence-holder shapes, catalog and token. Define precisely when legacy projections are emitted. Update checked Hello/Fenced formulas for the UUID/version fields, and name worst-view proto.Size and real Go/Rust transport fixtures at every new boundary.

findings.summary: Node.store_generation has no defined semantics despite being consumed as a security lifetime.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/design.md:126–133 appends store_generation and request/response generation fields without defining initialization, change conditions, monotonicity/overflow, preservation on label-only registration, or whether the two generations are identical. Current #52 contracts.md:43–56, 139–158 uses precisely #61 Node.store_generation in signed SourceProofV1 and source validation. An implementation cannot decide whether an old source token survives UUID A→B→A or enrollment/restart.
findings.fix: Define one source-lifetime generation authority, its exact stored/proto types and relationship to the replica gate and pagination generation. Specify atomic updates with UUID registration/enrollment, no-op preservation, ABA/overflow handling and field-level registration ownership (agents and other roles cannot supply/overwrite service-owned generations). Add registration/source-proof tests covering label CAS, restart, repeated UUID replacement and delayed proof replay.

findings.summary: The later VM reformat lab proof is incompatible with the current production clock-admission plan.
findings.evidence: docs/issues/61/intent.md, What we want 8, and design.md:169–172 prescribe the shared fl-a/fl-b VM lab as the later RF2 proof. Current #83 design.md:21–42 requires physical-boottime-v1 before storage opens and deliberately refuses these VMs; no force bypass exists.
findings.fix: Distinguish separately authorized pre-#83 exploratory VM evidence from supported production qualification, and provide an authorized physical-fixture alternative or explicitly mark that production proof unavailable under the VM lab. Do not invent physical attestations or broaden cloud/classification scope.

report: R1 security/spec-security review of the whole #61 intent/spec/design/decisions/issue-local ADR at 5696573a126c0abe26347d3c9700e557489613cf. Ten findings: 4 High, 5 Medium, 1 Low; not clear. The central store-bound invariant, token/current-epoch/first-epoch authorization before old-incarnation cleanup, no automatic force promotion, minimum-ISR preservation and conservative old-store release intent are sound. Existing token v2 does carry first_epoch; actual Hello cleanup is destructive before fencing, so ordering must remain explicit. Simulator/store-loss/identity-alias and bootstrap-old-token proof is required by the draft; every additional admission/completeness safety transition identified above also needs an explicit core check and caught mutant. No metadata/lock work was added to steady-state I/O by this review. All issue/dependency worktrees were clean and retained the recorded HEADs at final verification. No repository edits, tracker writes, runtime tests, benchmarks, shared VM or disk actions. Historical approvals remain evidence only; fixes and the proposed dedicated-root-cause split require fresh review/approval rather than fabricated acceptance.
